The ingest service runs in batch mode writing to clickhouse://oxhideset.analytics.events_raw, while the enrich service runs in stream mode writing to clickhouse://oxhideset.analytics.events_enriched. They differ in exactly two keys: mode (batch vs stream) and sink (events_raw vs events_enriched). Everything else matches: batch_rows 512 and an error.rate.threshold of 0.02 on both.

In net/backoff.py, a retry is triggered only by ThrottlingError: with_backoff calls op() up to attempts times (default 4), and whenever op() raises ThrottlingError it sleeps and tries again; any other exception propagates immediately. The starting delay is BASE_DELAY_MS = 250 ms, and the wait grows exponentially — the delay doubles after each failed attempt (250, 500, 1000 ms). If all attempts fail, it re-raises ThrottlingError("giving up").

The real trouble with the zone 3 valve V-3 started on 2026-07-19 at 04:10 with an open timeout FAULT, repeated at 04:25, and ended at 05:00 when the technician did a manual shutoff (logged OK). The technician's note says the V-3 solenoid stuck shut, and it was replaced on 2026-07-21. The two FAULT entries on 2026-07-21 marked MANUAL TEST were bench cycles in bypass with the valve already isolated, so they are not outage time.

The suspension began on 2026-06-23 at 11:52, when berth 2 winch W2 stopped and the log marked the berthing suspended (SUSPEND), after a pressure drop FAULT on W2 at 11:40. The failed winch was W2, and the NOTE finding at 14:05 was a hydraulic hose leak on W2, with the vessel diverted to the rail berth. W2's hose was replaced on 2026-06-24 with the load test passed, and the later W1 load-sensor FAULT on 2026-06-25 was just the known loose-connector glitch, cleared at 16:11 without suspending service.

The projector fault first showed up on 2026-08-01 at 21:40 as an ERROR with code LP-31, laser source current out of range, on screen 2's laser projector PL-700. The duty tech reseated the module at 21:44, but the same LP-31 fault returned on 2026-08-02 at 14:12. It was finally put right at 14:20 on 2026-08-02, when the module was replaced under warranty; the earlier FAN-1 WARNING was only advisory and cleared itself.

Riders were first left without bikes on 2026-08-23 at 10:15, when the Riverside Walk station went offline marked STOCKOUT. The gap ended at 13:05, when the station came back online with 12 bikes reloaded (OK). As for why it went offline in the first place, the log records it as a STOCKOUT, meaning the dock had no usable bikes for riders, and no equipment fault is named; the later 16:20 outage was only a planned DRILL exercise, which finished and put the station back online at 16:40.

The unplanned warmth in fridge VFT-2 started on 2026-09-04 at 13:20, when the logger recorded 9.8C above range as an EXCURSION, and it ended at 15:05 the same day with the temperature back in range at 4.6C (OK). The maintenance note blames the door seal: it had a gap that let warm air in, and the seal was replaced on the evening of 2026-09-04. The 8.9C reading on 2026-09-06 marked DEFROST is the fridge's scheduled monthly defrost cycle and is not an excursion.

The hoist gave out on 2026-08-19 at 11:15, when stage left hoist SL-2 logged a BREAKDOWN with the brake pads seized. The log had been warning about it before: two FAULT brake warnings on 2026-08-17 at 10:05 and 2026-08-18 at 19:40, each inspected. It was put right the same day: the seized brake pads were swapped and the hoist load-tested, and at 15:00 it was CLEARED and returned to service.
